solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One who needs roasting about absent archdeacon

indicators.note: the word for roasting is placed around the other pieces, as about can mean surrounding

parts.note: roasting means very hot
A is an abbreviation for absent or away
Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: Someone due a good grilling over a missing senior clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One who needs' is the whole definition: a poor person lacks things and so needs them.
explanation.definitionFit: A have-not is a person without wealth or possessions, someone in want of the basics.

clue.text: Vigorous lithe cat exercised

indicators.note: the letters of lithe cat are worked over, put through their paces into a new order

explanation.surface: A supple feline has been working out and is full of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an energetic, strong and active person or effort is athletic.

clue.text: Canine still also rising in early hours primarily

indicators.note: the other pieces sit in between the two initial letters
primarily asks for the first letters of early and hours

parts.note: still, as in 'still here', means yet

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for also is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: also means too

explanation.surface: A dog is still awake and getting up in the small hours.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'rising' means read upwards, so the word for also is turned round before joining the word for still between the two initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A canine tooth is the pointed one beneath the eye, popularly called the eye tooth.

clue.text: Have grocer to amend unreasonable price

indicators.note: to amend is to alter, so the letters of have grocer are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper is told to correct an excessive bill.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcharge is a demand for more money than is fair or due.

clue.text: Healthy hot beer

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A warm pint keeps one fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone hale is strong and in good health, as in 'hale and hearty'.

clue.text: Lady to damage bizarre hat

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil

indicators.note: bizarre means weird, so the letters of hat are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A woman sets out to wreck a strange piece of headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: Martha is a woman's name, so a lady can stand for it, as crosswords often allow.

clue.text: Last day of competition in outskirts of Slough

indicators.note: the word for competition goes in between the outer letters
outskirts are the edges of a town, so the first and last letters of Slough

parts.note: an event is a competition or contest

explanation.surface: The final day of a contest held on the edge of Slough, a town west of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last day of competition' reads as one phrase, but 'of' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible God rested on the seventh day, the last of the week, the Sabbath.

clue.text: Rope left in half of ditch next to American's garden

indicators.note: the letter for left goes inside the rest of the wordplay
next to sets the two pieces side by side
only half of the word for the ditch is used

parts.note: a ha-ha is a sunken ditch serving as a fence in a landscaped garden
Americans call a garden a yard

explanation.surface: A rope dropped into a ditch beside an American's back garden.
explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a sunken ditch with a wall on one side, keeping livestock out of a garden without blocking the view.
explanation.definitionFit: A halyard is a rope on a ship used to raise or lower a sail or flag.

clue.text: Dance with goddess around a bar

indicators.note: the goddess's name is wrapped around the other pieces

parts.note: Hera is the Greek queen of the gods
to bar is to ban or prohibit

explanation.surface: Dancing with a goddess around a pub counter.
explanation.definitionFit: The habanera is a slow Cuban dance, made famous by the aria in Bizet's Carmen.

clue.text: Anyone with gardening tool's almost green

parts.note: a hoe is a gardening tool for weeding

indicators.note: almost means the word for green loses its final letter

parts.note: vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: Anybody whose hoe is nearly green.
explanation.walkthrough: Vert, the heraldic word for green, loses its last letter. The 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: whoever means any person at all, as in 'whoever comes is welcome'.

clue.text: Unfortunately breathalysed with dabs roughly taken? Tough

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of breathalysed are jumbled
the letters of dabs are taken away, in no particular order, from that pool

explanation.surface: A driver is unluckily breath-tested and fingerprinted roughly: a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: Dabs is slang for fingerprints. Take D, A, B, S out of BREATHALYSED and rearrange the remaining RETHALYE.
explanation.definitionFit: Leathery meat or skin is tough and hard to chew or pierce, like leather.

clue.text: Legal expert acquiring rest house as property investment

indicators.note: the legal expert takes in the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: LLD is a Doctor of Laws
ease means rest or relaxation

explanation.surface: A lawyer takes on a rest home as an investment.
explanation.definitionFit: Leasehold property is held on a lease for a fixed term, a common kind of property investment.

clue.text: Bold commander embraces independence after that woman

indicators.note: the commander piece comes after the word for that woman

parts.note: that woman means her

indicators.note: the commander's letters hug the letter for independence

parts.note: OC is Officer Commanding

explanation.surface: A daring officer hugs independence, following a certain woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: heroic means brave and daring, as a hero is.

clue.text: Principal title held by Pole? Just the reverse

indicators.note: held by puts one piece inside another
the clue says the opposite is true, so the pole goes inside the title instead

parts.note: a header is a title at the top of a page
a mast is a pole, as on a ship

explanation.surface: A title held by a Polish person, or the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person but is a ship's pole. Read as given, the title would go inside; 'Just the reverse' swaps which piece holds which.
explanation.definitionFit: A headmaster is the principal of a school, the teacher in charge.

clue.text: 2 types; some strangely change shape at beginning of season

indicators.note: strangely means the letters of some are put in an odd order

parts.note: to morph is to change shape

indicators.note: takes the first letter of season

explanation.surface: Some people oddly change form as the season starts.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' points to the answer at 2-down, ATHLETIC: these are athletic body types.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesomorphs are people with a muscular, sturdy build, the sporty body type.

clue.text: Husband's popular — time to get intimate

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A well-liked husband finds the moment to get close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intimate' looks like an adjective about closeness; here it is a verb meaning to suggest.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimate is to suggest indirectly, just as to hint is.

clue.text: Controls runs round headland

indicators.note: the word for runs goes round the headland

parts.note: to hare is to run fast, so hares means runs
a ness is a headland, as in Dungeness on the Kent coast

explanation.surface: Someone controls a race around a coastal point.
explanation.definitionFit: To harness something is to control and use it, as with energy or a horse.

clue.text: Fish cast ashore in Kent, maybe

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go in the abbreviation

parts.note: Kent is a county in the south-east of England, so SE

indicators.note: cast means thrown about, so the letters of ashore are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fish washed up on a Kent beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A seahorse is a small upright fish with a horse-like head.

clue.text: I am in possession of your vitamin

indicators.note: the words I am are held inside the old word for your

parts.note: thine is an old form of your

explanation.surface: Someone claims to hold another person's vitamin pill.
explanation.definitionFit: Thiamine is vitamin B1, found in grains and needed for nerve function.

clue.text: Secretly kept stoats regularly in hut

indicators.note: the letters chosen go inside the word for hut

parts.note: a shed is a hut

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of stoats

explanation.surface: Stoats regularly hidden away in a garden hut.
explanation.definitionFit: To stash something is to hide it away in secret for later.

clue.text: Dimension of loaf that's half cut

parts.note: a loaf is bread

indicators.note: half of that is cut away, leaving its first two letters

explanation.surface: The size of a loaf that's been half sliced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it trims THAT to its first half; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadth is width, one of the measurements of an object.

clue.text: It's an imitation, not quite genuine, Oscar

indicators.note: not quite means the word for genuine falls short by its last letter

parts.note: echt is German for genuine, used in English
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A copy that is nearly real, named Oscar.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo repeats a sound, a copy of the original, so an imitation.

clue.text: Othello returns after Ron goes into the toilet?

indicators.note: the turned Othello piece comes after the first piece
Ron is put inside the word the
the word for Othello is read backwards

parts.note: Othello is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice

explanation.surface: Othello comes back after Ron has gone to the loo.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: throne is slang for a lavatory, so a room with one is a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A throne room is a royal chamber; humorously, the room with a slang throne is a lavatory.

clue.text: Name richest avoiding extremes in recessions

indicators.note: the outer letters of richest are left out

explanation.surface: Naming the wealthiest who escape the worst of economic slumps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recessions' suggests economic downturns but means alcoves.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a shallow recess in a wall, so recessions here are hollows.

clue.text: Not very bright chap could be hoaxed

indicators.note: could be means the letters of hoaxed may be rearranged into the answer

explanation.surface: A dim fellow might well be fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: Ox-head is an old insult for a dolt, a slow-witted person.

clue.text: Stiff leading actor (that Italian) died

parts.note: the star is the leading actor in a production
che is Italian for that

explanation.surface: The lead performer, that Italian, has passed away.
explanation.definitionFit: Starched fabric or manners are stiff, as a starched collar is.

clue.text: Print some sketches

indicators.note: some means only part of the word sketches is used

explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to make a print from a plate cut with acid.

clue.text: Record harim played for tribal leader

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: played means the letters of harim are performed in a new order

explanation.surface: A record of harem music played for the head of a tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephraim, son of Joseph, was founder of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.

clue.text: Dig in unusual tree in front of new church with name inscribed

indicators.note: in front of puts the first piece before the next ones
the letter for name is written into the jumbled tree
unusual means the letters of tree are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: An odd tree outside a new church has a name carved on it.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrench is to dig in, as soldiers do in trenches, or to establish firmly.

clue.text: Introduced the man with right to have second-hand clothing

indicators.note: clothing means the word for second-hand is wrapped around the others

parts.note: used means second-hand
he is the man

explanation.surface: A man is entitled to wear used clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' looks like a noun after 'second-hand' but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To usher someone in is to show or bring them in, so introduced.
